issues.evidence: Content now negotiates Flow health, contract 1.1.x, capabilities, and the providers[] readiness response before generation.
The background service worker persists every batch transition and owns start, resume, cancel, provider result, visual, and package progression.
Content Library receipts use content-library:// references; machine paths, provider session URLs, tokens, and image binary are excluded from durable JSON.

SEOSONA OS now publishes 13 atomic canonical claims from current official Google Search documentation, with source metadata, verification date, revalidation date, and tests that enforce reviewable records and verbatim claim mapping.
issues.gate: OS evidence packet tests 9/9 and Content strict cross-project audit 7/7.

issues.evidence: Live Flow contract 1.1.0, extension connection, project context, provider readiness, idempotency, and one real image were verified. The bridge still reports auth:none; quality backfill returned judged:false, and no authenticated Companion batch or five-package Content Library readback has completed.
issues.gate: Configure the same non-empty local MCP token in Flow and Companion, then complete and read back one live batch through Content.

issues.evidence: SEOSONA OS doctor now reports healthy; portable connector and security checks pass together with Content, Flow, and Video doctors.
Independent review found that factual copy could omit claims[]. A deterministic factual-signal gate now emits UNMAPPED_CLAIM, with a regression test for unsupported ranking guarantees.
Assets marked asset_needs_review are now archived with a receipt and stripped of inline binary instead of being discarded.
Companion responses and the orchestrator now whitelist only content-library:// package references, preventing runtime absolute paths from reaching Chrome storage or later batch.json files.
Flow MCP contract 1.1.0, quality normalization, quality backfill, persistence, and tests are committed in Flow commit f5044ae rather than remaining only in a dirty worktree.
Claim QA now requires semantic relation between each claim and its evidence record, and independently scans factual sentences for missing claim-map coverage.

Provider status is read from Chrome session storage before redispatch. Resume and result handling are serialized, concurrent resumes are deduplicated, and cancellation becomes durable before remote cleanup.
Quota, authentication, contract, provider-readiness, and Flow availability failures halt the batch without spending later draft work. The failed draft can be explicitly resumed after recovery.
The library package is written from the projected final state so batch.json contains the completed or needs_review result instead of a stale visual_running manifest.
Archived Flow exports require an approved image extension and are renamed from the validated asset id, preventing collision with draft.json or other package metadata.
facebook:verify:release invokes strict cross-project audit mode, which fails when the physical Video BrandKit or Flow MCP root is not supplied.
Evidence IDs no longer authorize lexical lookalikes. claims[].text must equal the canonical evidence claim and appear verbatim as an independent sentence in copy.
Visual completion checks current cancellation state after package I/O and before commit, so a late response cannot overwrite a durable cancelled batch.
Flow generation, quality retry, export, and archive run behind an idempotent asynchronous Companion job. Manifest V3 background uses short requests and chrome.alarms polling.
Provider preparing/running records now have a timeout lease and tab-liveness check; stale jobs become redispatchable with the same stable job ID.
Halt taxonomy includes WRONG_PROJECT plus Companion, asset archive, and Content Library failures, preventing later draft spend after infrastructure failure.
copyQa now records independent practical, evidence-led, clear, and respectful criteria and blocks deterministic brand voice violations.
V1 removed predicate-direction heuristics from authorization and requires the canonical evidence claim verbatim in copy, blocking both known and unseen antonym reversals.
Provider retry refreshes leaseUpdatedAt both when retry begins and after content-script acknowledgement; stale detection no longer uses only the first attempt timestamp.

SEOSONA Video now uses HyperFrames 0.7.104 and compatible companion packages. The production dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities; BrandKit validation, Video integration audit, doctor, HyperFrames check, and a strict ten-second MP4 render passed.
issues.gate: npm audit --omit=dev, brand:validate, video:audit:integration, seosona:doctor, HyperFrames check, and strict render smoke.

issues.evidence: Live generation exposed that MCP incorrectly required the user-facing Pipeline Queue toggle. Flow commit d7e6161 now requires only the loaded PromptQueue implementation; its regression test passed and the same stable client_ref generated one real image without enabling the UI toggle.

The owner's current dirty Flow worktree passes 1,376 of 1,380 unit tests. The four failures are repository-inventory, build-generated, inventory-reconciliation, and package-manifest reconciliation drift caused by the unmerged local file set; the Content Factory commits did not overwrite or absorb those changes.
issues.gate: After the current Flow changes are intentionally integrated, regenerate and review the tracked inventory/package artifacts, then rerun npm run test:unit.
